name: Kosaraju two-pass strongly connected components
definition: For G=(V,E), define G^T=(V,{(v,u):(u,v)∈E}). Run a complete DFS forest on G, append each vertex on exit to list L, then scan L in reverse; start DFS in G^T at each still unvisited vertex, ignoring vertices assigned in earlier second-pass trees. Each resulting tree is one strongly connected component
variables: V vertices, E directed arcs, G^T transpose, L increasing finishing order
assumptions: Finite directed graph with valid endpoints; both passes cover every vertex, with fresh visitation marks for the second pass; self-loops and parallel edges are harmless
limitations: O(|V|+|E|) time and storage including transpose; recursive DFS may exhaust the call stack on deep graphs; component labels and within-component order are not canonical
failure_conditions: Failure to reset visitation or to reverse the finish order
computation: Build adjacency lists for both orientations; first DFS records exit order, second DFS labels components. Empty graph yields an empty partition.

source.citation: Cornell CS 4120 (Spring 2023), Iterative solving, Strongly-connected components, https://courses.cs.cornell.edu/cs4120/2023sp/notes/iterative/index.html

name: Dinic layered blocking flow
definition: Initialize residual capacity r(u,v)=c(u,v), zero for absent arcs, and flow value F=0. BFS from s labels residual distances d. While t is reachable, keep edges with r(u,v)>0 and d(v)=d(u)+1. Repeatedly send δ=min residual capacity on a level-respecting s-to-t path; update r(u,v)=r(u,v)−δ, r(v,u)=r(v,u)+δ and F=F+δ until no such path remains. Rebuild BFS levels; terminate when t is unreachable
variables: c capacity, r residual capacity, s and t distinct terminals, d BFS distance, δ augmentation amount, F net flow value
assumptions: Finite directed graph, finite nonnegative capacities, exact arithmetic; combine parallel arcs by ordered endpoints and ignore self-loops; antiparallel arcs allowed in aggregated residual representation
limitations: At most |V|−1 blocking phases since shortest residual path length increases. Standard current-arc implementation takes O(|V|²|E|) time after excluding irrelevant isolated vertices and O(|V|+|E|) storage; a naive path enumerator need not achieve this bound. Numerical tolerance requires separate analysis
failure_conditions: Negative or nonfinite capacities or invalid endpoints
Incomplete blocking phase or missing reverse residual updates
computation: Construct residual adjacency including reverse arcs; compute BFS levels from source; use DFS with current-arc indices to saturate a blocking flow in each phase. Return F and optionally reachable side of the final cut.

source.citation: MIT 6.854, Strongly Polynomial Flow Algorithms, Scribe Notes #7, §3, https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.854/21/Scribe/s7-blockingFlows/unit-capacity.html (sink-oriented levels in source; equivalent source-oriented convention here).

name: Prim minimum spanning tree
definition: For connected undirected weighted G=(V,E), choose root r and initialize S={r}, T=∅. While S≠V, choose e=(u,v) of minimum weight among edges with u∈S and v∈V∖S; set T=T∪{e}, S=S∪{v}. Return T minimizing Σ_{e∈T}w(e)
variables: S growing vertex set, T selected tree edges, w finite edge weight, r starting vertex
assumptions: Finite nonempty connected undirected graph with finite real edge weights; negative and tied weights allowed; ignore loops, choose least parallel edge or retain parallel edges with identities
limitations: O((|V|+|E|)log|V|) time using indexed binary heap for |V|≥2, O(|V|+|E|) storage; disconnected graph requires explicit forest extension or rejection; tied weights may give multiple optimal trees
failure_conditions: Invalid weights, invalid endpoints or directed edges
No crossing edge while unvisited vertices remain
computation: Keep a minimum crossing-edge key and predecessor per unvisited vertex, update keys when a vertex enters S, and extract smallest key until all vertices are included. Single vertex yields empty tree.

source.citation: James S. Plank, University of Tennessee CS302, Minimum Spanning Tree, Prim’s Algorithm, https://web.eecs.utk.edu/~jplank/plank/classes/cs302/Notes/MST/; Duke COMPSCI 330 Lecture 14 (2019), cut property (parsed text; screenshot unavailable). Prim (1957) original paper locator not independently reviewed.

name: Bellman–Held–Karp subset dynamic programming
definition: Fix root r in a complete directed graph with n≥2 vertices and finite costs c(i,j). For r∈S⊆V and j∈S∖{r}, D({r,j},j)=c(r,j), and D(S,j)=min_{i∈S∖{r,j}}[D(S∖{j},i)+c(i,j)] for |S|>2. The optimal rooted tour cost is min_{j∈V∖{r}}[D(V,j)+c(j,r)]
variables: V vertex set, n size, r root, S visited subset, j terminal vertex, D minimum path cost for exactly S, c additive directed edge cost
assumptions: Complete finite directed cost matrix, fixed additive costs independent of history; exact arithmetic; negative and asymmetric costs allowed because each vertex visited exactly once before closing tour
limitations: O(n²2^n) time and O(n2^n) table storage with constant-time subset indexing and arithmetic; exponential resource requirements; not the Held–Karp relaxation or approximation
failure_conditions: Root absent, n<2 for this specification, subset indexing overflow or resource budget exceeded
computation: Evaluate states by increasing subset size, store minimizing predecessor if reconstructing a tour, then add closing edge and minimize. Validate resource limits before allocation.

source.citation: Carnegie Mellon University 15-451 (Fall 2023), Dynamic Programming II, §1, pp. 1–3, https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~15451-f23/lectures/lecture10-dp2.pdf. Held and Karp (1962) original publication locator not independently reviewed.
